description: Minimal public decision snapshots. No hidden tiles, identity, session metadata, future outcomes, or full game log. Case IDs preserve source serials only for reproducible evidence mapping.

cases.notes: A quiet second discard has 35 versus 44 structural improving tiles; a stage cap must not make them equal.
The weaker immediate ukeire route can improve shape on the next draw; direct improvements alone do not order two-draw progress.
Retaining 3p gives concrete 345p and 567s improvements; compare actual reachable routes across shanten depths.
A formal one-shanten route lacks an immediate yaku wait; retreating to two shanten must not acquire an unrelated optimistic yaku prior.
Honor retention has a concrete yakuhai route despite lower structural ukeire; a higher-ukeire honor discard is not a universal target.
The first 2p pon improves ordinary structure without establishing a yaku; compare concrete open and closed continuation assumptions.
Calling 7s permits a toitoi route when suited singles are discarded; the later actual discard is not a recommendation label.
After the 7s pon, retaining pairs can preserve toitoi while a formal 36s wait remains without yaku.
A 1s pon creates a scored six-han toitoi wait; confirmed scoring must override the coarse open-yaku prior and avoid a false no-yaku penalty.
The concrete post-pon 4s discard is paired with the preceding call case to check yaku and action-cost consistency.
The early 7s discard is genbutsu to the newly declared dealer riichi; preserve valid defensive reasons to retain an isolated honor.
